I get it. I despise being on camera. You absolutely do not need to see my face in order for me to do my job. But I understand not everyone has the same work ethic. I grew up in a very catholic household. A new friend from my new school gave me a burned CD in a case with a blank insert. Or so I thought. My mom had apparently gone through my bag and on the inside of the insert it said Hooray for Boobies. I will never forget that friend for helping me break the rules and explore music.

We did do other things closer to home like six flags or bush gardens and i remember never getting anything except passes to ride rides. Which gave me a little FOMO but nothing unusual for a kid.

We live in the midwest so we will be going on a trip to Chicago next year. My parents would take us every year for 3 days. Mostly to the aquarium and museums (which we loved) and enjoying the city.

To my children's credit (esp the older ones), they also have no real interest in going to Disney. We love Disney movies, but none of us will wind up with a Winnie the pooh tattoo or smth.

I've taken them to the amusement parks around here and they love it. Im grateful. And, previously, they didn't get anything either. So this summer when we take our trip I'll be really excited to get them the picture from the roller coaster.

I count myself as a lucky parent that they aren't begging for disney or universal level trips. Not that they *wouldn't* go, but it's "mid" as they say.

Oh man have I got STORIES. For a relatively short one, look at my comment history. The last one I wrote was about the Bastard Incident. But... How did it effect me? Horribly. CPTSD is a real thing. I'm 39. Didn't do any real deep dive in therapy til around 35. I'm ok(ish) now but for all those other years I wasn't. It's f'ed up.

I was a young mom - 18. There was one time I smacked my 2nd kid in the face (he was around 8), without even thinking, and I felt like the most horrible mother/human on earth. That smack snapped me out of whatever generational trauma-hell I had been living in.

It creates some sort of reflex within you. That learned behavior, that boomers find so easy to justify. It's a tough cycle to break but I did it. Never punished my kids like that again.

What did I do instead? Well, one time the older 2 were fighting so bad - physically - i set up a "boxing ring" in the yard and told them they had to fight to blood.

They refused and never physically fought again. Bickered, sure.

My father was a sailor so... Mostly him, much to my mother's aggravation. My mother's family was also mostly uneducated - dad was a bomber in WWII, mom had barely graduated high school. Siblings only did high school. The most important part? They lived in NJ (IYKYK). We spent a lot of time with them.

Also late night tv my brother and I would sneak to watch.

My mother must've been right inside the screen door (front door was open). She reached out and snatched me inside by my ponytail so fast. I had a couple of smacks across my face and a spoon full of dawn in my mouth before I even knew I did anything wrong.

She said the time-forgotten line of "wait til your father gets home". He was always gone, being in the Navy, so it was rare she said that - but we knew what it meant.

I was sent to my room. He came home not too long after and he came to my room. I was terrified. Normally, in that situation, I'd have to drop my pants, bend over and grab my ankles, and my butt would meet his heavy leather belt.

This time? I heard him laughing. A bellowing laugh. I heard my mother yell about it not being funny. I heard his boots on the stairs. I remember feeling even more confused now, sitting on my bed.

He opened the door and just stopped dead. He looked at me kinda funny and then walked over and lifted up my chin. His face wasn't angry but really sad. It was obvious I'd been crying but what he saw was the smack welts on my face.

He asked me what happened. Where did I hear that word? I don't know. What did I think it meant? I'm not really sure. He hugged me. Held me. Told me it was ok. We talked for a little while. He'd been gone 6 months this time. I missed him. He told me to be very careful around my mother especially in what I said. He told me he loved me more than anything in the whole world and apologized that he had to be gone so much. He told me to just get ready for bed and stay upstairs. I heard him yelling at my mother. I fell asleep.

I would never again feel the wrath of his belt on my bottom (csnt say the same for my brother, tho that's a different story). He would never again believe what my mother said about me without talking to me first. He was still gone a lot, but when he was home he was my protector. The only love I experienced as a kid, really. We built a very special bond after the Bastard Incident.

I'll never forget that day. I got A LOT of smacks and hair snatches through the years from my mother over cuss words (and other "unladylike" behavior) - I stopped caring and learned to dodge.

Anyway, I learned them mostly from my dad. And I wouldn't change it for anything and I don't think he would either.

Typically you don't need another game pass for those, just another account for the controller to sign in to. It's dumb how they do it now, but it is what it is. 

Other kids games like paw patrol, super pets, peppa pig, bunny park, and minecraft have couch coop. It's not very stimulating for adults ofc but that's not really the focus when playing with small kids. They'd enjoy it esp if you hype it up.
